title: First Ten Iterations: Fast Feedback Onboarding (scratch)
content:
Context
---
This is a personal scratchpad for an experiment-first onboarding flow aimed at enabling product and platform teams to ship 10 small, observable feature experiments in the first week after kickoff. Target users are PMs/engineers who want to validate hypothesis quickly on hosted-api without long infra work.

Goals (high-level)
1) Reduce time-to-first-observable-experiment from ~2w to <48h.
2) Provide automated telemetry and guardrails so a non-platform engineer can run an A/B or sample rollout safely.
3) Capture a repeatable checklist and lightweight templates for first-ten experiments.

Why now
- Many teams waste cycles on infra/permission/config and instrumentation for first experiments.
- If we can lower friction, more teams will use Redwood Hosted API for early validation and convert to Dedicated/Private later.

Core idea (one-liner)
A tiny onramp product toolkit (templates + CLI + dashboard snippet + prewired telemetry) that scaffolds the first 10 experiments, automates safety checks, and surfaces results in a single page.

What counts as an "iteration"
- Small scope: new response tweak, fallback policy change, or simple routing rule.
- Runs against real traffic with controlled sampling or synthetic traffic.
- Instrumented with request/response observability (latency, cost/tokens, model output quality via prompt checks).
- Has clear success metric and a decision: roll, refine, or kill.

Rough flow (happy path)
1) PM creates "Experiment" from UI or CLI: name, hypothesis, primary metric, sampling rate, start/end.
2) System creates experiment-id, generates a minimal config (route, model variant if needed, prompt template) and a telemetry dashboard stub.
3) User toggles to deploy sample (5-20%) with safety caps (cost cap, latency threshold, profanity/unsafe output detector).
4) Telemetry streams incremental evaluation: side-by-side baseline vs experiment (CTR-like metric or qualitative check).
5) At end of window user picks action (promote/adjust/stop).

Requirements (MVP)
- Templates: 5 prebuilt experiment templates (prompt tweak, fallback reorder, cheap-variant routing, prefix-caching toggle, response-length cap).
- CLI command: redwood experiment new --template X --metric "helpful_rate" --sample 0.1
- Dashboard stub with: sample size, token-cost delta, latency delta, baseline vs variant metric, basic content-safety alerts.
- Safety: default cost cap per experiment (e.g., $100/day), default 20% sample cap, automatic model fallback if latency > SLO.
- Instrumentation: event tagging (experiment_id) on every request, automatic A/B labeling in logs/traces.

User stories
- As a PM, I want a template for "response conciseness" so I can test shorter outputs without editing infra.
- As an engineer, I want a CLI that scaffolds the route and sample traffic so I don't have to touch k8s or infra.
- As a data analyst, I want clean experiment_id tags so I can query results in analytics and build quick charts.

Success metrics (for platform team)
- Time-to-first-experiment (median) < 48h for 90% of adopters.
- % experiments that reach decision (promote/kill/iterate) within 7 days > 60%.
- No infra incidents caused by experiments in first 3 months.

Instrumentation detail (notes to self)
- Tagging: request.headers[X-Experiment-Id], request.metadata.experiment = id (if possible).
- Add an experiment column to token billing stream for per-experiment cost.
- Quick quality eval: simple heuristics (exact-match golden tokens, length delta, profanity detector); support plug-in evals later.

Rollout plan (staged)
- Alpha: internal product/platform teams only, manual review, limited to 5 templates.
- Beta: select customers + opt-in, add self-serve UI.
- GA: public, with per-org quota controls and audit log export.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Sampling model: should we prefer deterministic hashing by user_id or random sample? (deterministic simplifies user-level comparisons but complicates repeated experiments).
- Cost caps: how strict? Refund or auto-stop when cap hit? (prefer auto-stop + email).
- Safety checks: rely on our content-safety service or let users opt-out for internal experiments? (default enforce).
- How to support experiments that need nontrivial infra (stateful steps, session-level flows)? MVP should avoid session state changes.

Instrumentation snippet (UX)
- Quick button in Console: "New quick experiment" -> small modal: name/hypothesis/metric/sample/cost cap -> generate -> view dashboard.
- CLI maps to same flow; prints experiment-id and a link to dashboard.

Experiment templates (MVP list)
1) Concise answers: prompt wrapper to limit tokens / ask for bullets.
2) Humble fallback reorder: change primary->fallback ordering with canned fallbacks.
3) Cheap-route: route to a lower-cost quantized variant for 50% of requests.
4) Rate-limit for long responses: apply soft cap and measure helpful_rate.
5) Prefix caching on popular queries: enable prefix cache for 10 query keys and measure latency/cost.

Data schema (minimum)
- experiment_id (string)
- variant (control|variant)
- sample_rate (float)
- cost_estimate_usd (float)
- metric_value (float or boolean)
- created_by (string)
- started_at, ended_at

Experiment template example (Concise answers)
- CLI: redwood experiment new --template concise --metric helpful_rate --sample 0.1 --cap 75
- Generated config: route /v1/rl/answer?exp_id=exp_abc123 -> model: gpt-open-7b-quant -> prompt-wrapper: "Respond in <= 60 words; bullet list if >1 item"

Monitoring and alerting
- Alert if variant latency p95 > baseline p95 + 200ms for more than 10m.
- Alert if content-safety hits exceed 0.1% of sample for more than 5m.
- Cost alert when cumulative experiment cost > 80% of cap.

Parking lot (ideas to revisit)
- Auto-generated evaluation prompts from user-provided examples.
- Experiment marketplace: share small experiment recipes across orgs (sanitized).
- Integration with rollout: automatic promote to route if experiment improves metric by statistical significance.
- Quick ablation tools: run N small ablations of prompt parameters in parallel.

Immediate next steps (for me)
- Sketch minimal UI wireframe and CLI UX (today).
- Draft protobuf for experiment tag in telemetry stream (this week).
- Quick meeting with Rowan + Asha to sync on template list (mon).
- Build alpha checklist and pair with platform engineer for a 2-week spike.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep templates intentionally opinionated; too flexible = support burden.
- We need a single canonical experiment-id propagated everywhere. No ad-hoc labels.
- This should integrate cleanly into the Console "Experiments" tab (future).

Links / references
- Slack thread: #prod-experiments (see message thread on 2024-10-21)
- Similar internal doc: confluence:mini-experiments-ops (read for instrumentation ideas)

Unresolved
- Who owns promoting experiment to production? PM or infra? Likely PM with a guardrail requiring infra sign-off for model upgrades.

End.
